companyDescription: Cell therapy · Deramiocel — allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, first-in-class mechanism awaiting its second FDA decision
priceNote: Live $5.83 (-1.7%) at Oct 26, 2026 open — down ~41% from $9.91 at the Sep 29 report; 52-week range $2.96-$40.37. Market cap ~$339M. Since the Sep 29 reports, this board's small caps fell 21-41% after the Sep 16 hike and the hot Sep CPI (Oct 14). This is a sector/size selloff that SPY-based regime notes don't capture, so drawdowns here say as much about the tape as the thesis.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Sep 29, 2026): the Nov 22, 2026 PDUFA for deramiocel (refined to an upper-limb-function DMD indication, the HOPE-3 primary endpoint) is unchanged. The stock lost ~41% into it as securities suits over the early-September disclosure accumulated. New HOPE-3 open-label data (76% slowing of upper-limb decline after switching from placebo) and a B. Riley upgrade to Buy ($21) are the offsets. fda_decision is a Tier-2 LEADER (+9.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=10). But the July adcomm voted 9-3 against efficacy on the original cardiomyopathy ask, so this is not a clean approval bet. Base cut from +90% to +70% (above the lane's realized 30d P90 of +25.9%; written-Base bias +72.7pp). It assumes approval on Nov 22 and a ~1-3 month re-rating back to the ~$9.91 Sep level. แนะนำ 2-3% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้าโดน CRL ลงได้ 50%+.

catalysts.name: Deramiocel PDUFA decision — upper-limb function indication
catalysts.description: FDA target action date for the amended BLA, narrowed to upper-limb function (PUL 2.0 primary endpoint) after the Jul 29-30, 2026 adcomm voted 9-3 against the original DMD-cardiomyopathy claim but gave directionally supportive feedback on this narrower endpoint.

risks: FDA advisory committee voted 9-3 against efficacy for the original DMD-cardiomyopathy indication (Jul 2026, non-binding). The narrowed upper-limb indication is a reasonable fix, but approval is far from assured.
Securities class actions over the early-September 2026 data disclosure are an overhang independent of the FDA outcome and have accompanied a ~41% decline since Sep 29.
A second CRL (after the Jul 2025 CRL, -33% day-1) would likely retest or break the ~$4.19 post-adcomm low and force a dilutive raise.
The narrowed indication caps the addressable population and peak sales versus the original ask, even if approved.
Launch risk if approved: payer coverage for a novel cell therapy, physician adoption, and manufacturing scale-up.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE · Moonshot 2.5% max (refreshed Oct 26) — the Nov 22 PDUFA is intact and the stock is 41% cheaper, but the 9-3 adcomm vote and litigation make this a genuinely two-sided binary. Measured turbo at-catalyst median is -13.7% (n=19), so Entry 2 ($5.00-5.40) is preferred and Entry 1 is a starter only.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Reverse run-up: CAPR fell ~41% since Sep 29 into its Nov 22 PDUFA as securities suits over the early-September data disclosure piled up — the opposite of a typical pre-PDUFA drift.

postWin.note: CAPR's own Dec 2025 Phase 3 HOPE-3 readout is the most direct precedent: the stock ran from $6.36 to $40.37 (+300%) in two trading days on positive DMD cell-therapy data. A November approval likely produces a smaller pop than a surprise data win — some of it is now pre-priced after the recovery to ~$9.91 and the adcomm's supportive upper-limb commentary — but the name has proven capable of 3x-type moves on this exact drug/indication.

postLose.note: CAPR's own Jul 30, 2026 reaction to the FDA adcomm's 9-3 negative vote is the direct precedent: the stock fell 36% in one day ($6.57 to $4.19). A second rejection/CRL on the narrowed upper-limb indication in November would likely be at least as severe, possibly worse given it would be the drug's second regulatory setback.

spotSizing.reason: 2.5%. fda_decision is a Tier-2 LEADER (+9.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=10), but the July adcomm voted 9-3 against efficacy on the original indication, and the stock has de-rated 41% into the date. The weak lane scoreboard (hitRate 4.9%, n=41) caps it here.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the fda_decision medianMAE (-18.4%, n=10). A break below ~$4.55 before Nov 22 suggests the market is pricing a second CRL.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If FDA issues a second CRL, exit on day 1 — the 2025 CRL precedent was -33% in one session.

comparableCases.event: Elevidys FDA accelerated approval (first DMD gene therapy)
comparableCases.note: First DMD gene therapy approval — but the restrictive label (ages 4-5, ambulatory only, versus the broader ask) triggered an 11% same-day drop despite the approval itself, a reminder that a narrow-label 'win' can still disappoint. CAPR's own narrowed upper-limb-only ask carries similar risk.

catalysts.name: คำตัดสิน PDUFA ของ Deramiocel — ข้อบ่งใช้ upper-limb function
catalysts.description: วันตัดสินของ FDA สำหรับ BLA ที่แก้ไขแล้ว เหลือแค่ข้อบ่งใช้ upper-limb function (PUL 2.0) หลัง adcomm วันที่ 29-30 ก.ค. 2026 โหวต 9-3 คว่ำข้อบ่งใช้ cardiomyopathy เดิม แต่ให้ความเห็นสนับสนุนในทาง endpoint ที่แคบลงนี้

risks: คณะกรรมการที่ปรึกษา FDA โหวต 9-3 ไม่เห็นด้วยกับประสิทธิผลในข้อบ่งใช้ DMD-cardiomyopathy เดิม (ก.ค. 2026, ไม่ผูกมัด) การจำกัดข้อบ่งใช้เหลือแขนเป็นทางแก้ที่สมเหตุสมผล แต่ยังไม่การันตีการอนุมัติ
คดีหลักทรัพย์จากการเปิดเผยข้อมูลต้น ก.ย. 2026 เป็นแรงกดดันแยกจากผล FDA และมาพร้อมการร่วง ~41% นับจาก 29 ก.ย.
ถ้าโดน CRL ครั้งที่สอง (หลัง CRL ก.ค. 2025 ที่ -33% ในวันเดียว) น่าจะทดสอบหรือหลุดจุดต่ำหลัง adcomm ~$4.19 และต้องเพิ่มทุน
ข้อบ่งใช้ที่แคบลงจำกัดจำนวนผู้ป่วยและยอดขายสูงสุดเทียบกับข้อเสนอเดิม แม้จะได้รับอนุมัติ
ความเสี่ยงการเปิดตัวหากอนุมัติ: การเบิกจ่ายของ payer สำหรับ cell therapy ใหม่ การยอมรับของแพทย์ และการขยายการผลิต
